🔻 Iran criticizes US congressional hearing for ignoring human cost of war

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei has criticized a US congressional hearing on the performance of the country’s secretary of war during the conflict with Iran, saying American lawmakers failed to address the humanitarian consequences of Washington’s military campaign.

In a post on X on Wednesday night, Baqaei described it as a shame that the hearing focused solely on the financial costs of the conflict without raising a single question about the human dimension of the war.
​
“It’s a shame that throughout the US Secretary of War’s congressional hearing, not a single question was asked regarding the “human” aspect of America’s ruthless war against the Iranian nation, fully aware that this was an illegal war of choice accompanied by countless war crimes, Minab and Lamerd being just two of them,” the spokesperson said.
​
On Tuesday, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth testified before the Senate about the financial cost of the war against Iran, as he called for nearly $70 billion in additional funding for the conflict.
​
On February 28, 2026, the first day of the recent US-Israeli war, a missile strike destroyed Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab, Hormuzgan Province, killing at least 168 people including schoolchildren. The same day, strikes on civilian locations, including a school and a sports hall, killed at least 21 people in the city of Lamerd, Fars Province. Women and children were among the victims of the attack in Lamerd, also located in the south.

🔊 Former Iranian foreign minister to Americans: Save your children from Trump’s quagmire

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Manouchehr Mottaki, former Iranian foreign minister and Member of Parliament representing Tehran, has addressed the American people, saying: “Thousands of American troops stationed at military bases in the Persian Gulf states, Jordan, and Iraq are currently within range of Iranian missiles. I advise you to bring them home today, so that tomorrow you will not be deprived of the chance to mourn your sons.”

In an interview with IRNA, Mottaki said: “Your shortsighted president, Donald Trump, and the invading American military have, through the imposition of two criminal wars, martyred more than 1,000 Iranians. The Iranian nation mourns the nation’s martyred Leader and his children.”
​
The former foreign minister added: “For the past 140 nights, the Iranian people have held nightly gatherings in squares and streets across the country, angrily demanding the country’s military commanders avenge the blood of the martyrs by taking action against the American-Zionist terrorists.”
​
Addressing the American people, Mottaki said: “Thousands of US troops stationed at military bases in the Persian Gulf states, Jordan, and Iraq are now within range of Iranian missiles. At any moment, in response to the Iranian nation’s demand, an order may be issued to launch strikes that could kill more than 1,000 of those criminal soldiers.”
​
He concluded with a warning: "Bring your sons home today, before tomorrow arrives when you receive their remains. By Trump’s order, their deaths may never even be publicly acknowledged, depriving you of the opportunity to mourn them.”

🌍 Advisor to Leader: Iran’s new phase of deterrence means attacks will not come at low cost

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Ali Akbar Velayati, senior adviser to the Leader of the Islamic Revolution on international affairs, has warned that the notion that striking Iran would come at little cost is a mistake whose consequences could extend far beyond the military sphere, as the country has strengthened its deterrence.

In a post on X on Wednesday, Velayati said Iran has entered a new phase of deterrence, stressing that any attack on Iran could have repercussions extending beyond the battlefield and spilling over into global energy markets and the world economy.
​
He also cautioned the White House against threatening Iran, mobilizing its regional allies and activating European lobbying efforts.
​
“The White House should understand that threatening Iran, mobilizing its regional allies and activating the European lobby will not bring greater security or stability; rather, it will globalize the consequences of its mistakes.”
